result.title: Rethinking Agent Trajectory Compression: A Workflow-Aware Perspective
result.summary: As long-horizon agents increasingly rely on multi-step tool interactions to accomplish complex tasks, their execution trajectories continuously accumulate structured outputs and intermediate artifacts, leading to growing context overhead. Existing compression methods primarily rely on text importance or fixed truncation rules, often overlooking cross-step dependencies within workflows and potentially discarding critical information required for subsequent task execution. To address this challenge, we propose WAAC, a workflow-aware framework for agent trajectory compression. WAAC structurally models successful historical trajectories to extract reusable workflow compression experience and incorporates online backward dependency analysis to dynamically identify information retention requirements. By combining current dependency constraints with historical experience, WAAC selects appropriate compression strategies for different types of historical information. Experiments on PinchBench and Odysseys demonstrate that WAAC achieves an overall score of 87.6 and a perfect completion rate of 19.0%, respectively, while reducing execution costs by 19.7% and 29.1% compared with the strongest baseline methods. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of workflow-aware trajectory compression in improving task performance and cost efficiency for long-horizon agents. Code and resources are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/waac-6527/.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究长程工具型 agent 的执行轨迹上下文膨胀问题，提出 WAAC 框架：从历史成功轨迹中抽取可复用的 workflow 压缩经验，并结合在线反向依赖分析动态确定各步信息需保留的要求，据此为不同历史信息选择压缩策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「反向依赖决定信息保留」的思路可能为 LVR 中哪些中间证据需留在 latent 状态、如何筛选视觉/中间信息提供可核查线索，但对象是纯文本 agent 轨迹，需确认能否迁移到多模态推理状态维护。
